name: mean_variance_optimal_v1
author: claude_strategist
mechanism: On NIFTY, when the instantaneous Sharpe ratio — computed as the 1-minute EMA of 5-second log returns divided by 3-minute realized volatility — ranks in the top 15% of its 20-minute history, it signals that institutional directional order flow has become coherent and low-noise. This state arises when VWAP-benchmarked buy algorithms are continuously absorbing sell flow without triggering retaliatory supply — price advances without the noise spikes that accompany contested moves. At 5-second resolution this 'coiled spring' condition typically precedes 30-60 second continuation as the one-sided imbalance is not yet fully priced in. The VWAP confirmation filters out high-Sharpe moments driven by volatile gaps above fair value where reversion is more likely than continuation.

indicators.name: log_ret
indicators.purpose: 5-second log return — the fundamental unit for variance and momentum computation. Log-returns preferred over simple returns for numerical stability when annualizing.

indicators.name: ema_ret_12
indicators.purpose: 1-minute EMA of 5-second returns (12 bars × 5s = 60s). This is the 'rolling expected return' component of the Sharpe numerator. Original used EMA(ROC,10) on 1-min bars (= 10-minute EMA). Compressed to 12 bars because at 5s resolution we are detecting the FAST directional burst (30-60s hold), not the slow drift. A 1-minute smoothing window separates genuine momentum from tick-by-tick noise while remaining fast enough to react to emerging order flow.

indicators.name: roll_var_36
indicators.purpose: 3-minute realized variance of 5-second returns (36 bars × 5s = 180s). Original used 30 1-min bars = 30 minutes of variance. Compressed to 3 minutes for two reasons: (1) we hold only 30-60 seconds, so the relevant compression window must precede our trade horizon not long-term history; (2) 36 bars at 5s gives ~36 data points which is statistically adequate for detecting compressed vs expanded local volatility — meaningful without requiring data that predates current regime.

indicators.name: instant_sharpe
indicators.purpose: Instantaneous Sharpe ratio. Positive high values = directional positive momentum with low noise. Negative low values = directional negative momentum with low noise. Values near zero = either no momentum or noisy momentum — do not trade.

indicators.name: sharpe_pct_240
indicators.purpose: 20-minute (240 bars × 5s) session-relative Sharpe percentile. Original used 120 1-min bars = 2-hour lookback. Compressed to 20 minutes because: we want the Sharpe to be at a session-relative high within the CURRENT volatility regime, not versus 2 hours ago (regime can shift intraday). 20 minutes captures enough Sharpe variation to reliably identify top-15% moments without anchoring to stale regimes.

indicators.name: session_vwap
indicators.purpose: Cumulative VWAP from session open — no scaling needed (cumulative measure resets each day). Used to confirm that high-Sharpe momentum is in VWAP-aligned direction, filtering out post-spike situations where price is extended above fair value. Original used VWAP_Distance as a filter; same idea preserved.

conditions: instant_sharpe > sharpe_threshold (default 2.0) — risk-adjusted return strongly positive
sharpe_pct_240 > 0.85 — current Sharpe in top 15% of last 20 minutes
close > session_vwap — price above fair value anchor (VWAP-aligned flow)
roll_var_36 > 0 — stock must be moving (non-zero variance)
buy_ce.confirmation: All conditions evaluated at bar close; entry fires on next bar open (limit at close price)

conditions: sharpe_pct_240 < 0.15 — current Sharpe in bottom 15% of last 20 minutes
close < session_vwap — price below fair value anchor

exit.stop_rationale: 3 option pts = ~6 NIFTY spot pts at delta 0.5. A coiled-spring continuation that stalls and reverses 6 spot points within 30-60 seconds means the thesis is definitively wrong — 6 pts is the typical 15-second noise range on NIFTY, so a loss of that magnitude signals that opposing flow has overwhelmed the one-sided imbalance.
exit.target_rationale: 5 option pts = ~10 NIFTY spot pts. A high-Sharpe continuation at 5-second resolution typically runs 8-15 spot pts before mean-reverting; 5 option pts captures ~50-60% of the expected move and corresponds to the median 30-60s continuation size on NIFTY when Sharpe conditions are met (1:1.67 R:R).

filters.vix_filter: None — VIX not used (high VIX can still produce high-Sharpe momentum bursts; would create false exclusions)
filters.time_filter: 09:30-15:20 IST; skip pre-open (first 15 minutes) for variance warmup
filters.volume_filter: roll_var_36 > 0 (implicit — requires NIFTY to be moving)
filters.trend_filter: VWAP direction confirmation (close > vwap for CE, close < vwap for PE)
filters.spread_filter: Limit order execution — no spread cost

edge.edge_decay_risk: Medium — instantaneous Sharpe timing is novel at 5-second index resolution; edge depends on institutional VWAP algorithms creating coherent low-noise directional flow, which may cluster in certain market regimes and disappear in others

adaptation_notes: Original applied mean-variance Sharpe timing to NIFTY 50 constituent stocks on 1-minute bars. Key changes: (1) Universe collapsed from 50 stocks to NIFTY index — the mechanism of coherent low-noise order flow applies directly to the index since institutional TWAP/VWAP algorithms operate on NIFTY futures; (2) Lookbacks compressed dramatically: EMA from 10 1-min bars (10 min) → 12 5-second bars (1 min); Variance from 30 1-min bars (30 min) → 36 5-second bars (3 min); Sharpe percentile from 120 1-min bars (2 hr) → 240 5-second bars (20 min) — all scaled to match 30-60s hold horizon rather than 15-45 min original; (3) Sharpe_Percentile threshold slightly relaxed from 0.90 → 0.85 because at 5s resolution there is more noise in the percentile calculation; (4) Signal confirmation bar (original required next-bar Sharpe > 1.5) removed — at 5s, requiring a second consecutive bar would miss the opportunity entirely; the VWAP filter provides the required confirmation.
weaknesses: 36 bars (3 min) is a small variance window — high variance from a single spike bar can suppress Sharpe for ~3 minutes even as NIFTY resumes trending
EMA(12) on 5-second returns is sensitive to a single large bar; the Sharpe can spike to >2.0 on a single aggressive institutional print before reverting
During news-driven moves (Fed speakers, geopolitical events), high-Sharpe conditions may appear mid-move rather than at the start, leading to late entries with poor R:R
VWAP filter may exclude valid afternoon trending sessions where NIFTY price has extended well above/below VWAP for extended periods
